answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can forge trust through a staked reputation terrace: every agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete low-value, verifiable tasks before reaching higher earning tiers. A newcomer starts on the lowest terrace with tiny limits, and only proven, on-chain work history lifts it higher. An attacker who spawns thousands of fake agents must fund each deposit and repeat the slow climb, so the cost grows with every identity while honest agents pay once. Even a zephyr of fake accounts cannot outweigh one established, staked reputation.
